summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with fevers, chills, left flank pain, and a dislodged percutaneous nephrostomy (PCN) tube, following several weeks of cloudy, foul-smelling urine. He had recently completed a course of meropenem for a prior kidney infection. The PCN tube was replaced in the ED, and he was started on IV meropenem for pyelonephritis. Urine cultures from the PCN site initially grew E. coli, which was sensitive to meropenem; subsequent cultures showed no growth, indicating treatment success. An MRI of the left hip was performed due to concern for osteomyelitis from a chronic ulcer, but findings were consistent with reactive changes rather than bone infection, so no additional antibiotics were given. The patient declined professional wound care and opted to manage the ulcer himself. He also reported maroon blood in loose stools; rectal exam revealed hemorrhoids and prolapse without active bleeding, and no C. diff testing was completed due to inadequate sample. His chronic kidney disease remained stable, though phosphorus was elevated, suggesting a need for sevelamer dose adjustment post-discharge. He completed a 10-day course of meropenem and was discharged home on his prior medications, including oxycodone and fosfomycin, with naloxone provided for overdose prevention. Follow-up was arranged with nephrology, urology, and primary care.
